## Requirement

When a Case linked to an Account is escalated (Case.IsEscalated becomes true), automatically email the Account Owner so they are aware their customer is unhappy; the email includes the Case Number and Subject. Delivered as a single after-save record-triggered Flow on Case, design-only (no org access), scale: feature due to two named objects (Case, Account).

## Scope

### In scope

- Send an automated email to the Account Owner whenever a Case on that Account is escalated (Case.IsEscalated transitions to true), including the Case Number and Subject in the email (Q1, requirement statement).
- Fire on every new transition into escalated, including a repeat escalation after a Case was previously un-escalated, not only the first-ever escalation (Q1).
- Handle the no-related-Account and no-person-Owner (Queue-owned Account) edge cases explicitly rather than letting them fail silently: skip-and-log for no Account, fall back to the Support Manager distribution list when the owner is a Queue (Q3).
- A fault path that logs any send failure and notifies the Salesforce admin distribution list (Q4).

### Out of scope

- Building or modifying native Salesforce Escalation Rules (the mechanism that sets IsEscalated in the first place) — the requirement only asks to react to an escalation that already happens; confirmed no engine change is requested and the native engine's own notify actions cannot target a dynamically-resolved Account Owner (see D1 rationale).
- Any change to Case routing/assignment on creation — out of scope; not mentioned in the requirement and no clarification implied it.
- In-app bell / SMS / Slack notification channels — the requirement asks specifically for email (Q11 default); other channels are a separate ask.
- Reporting or a dashboard on escalation notifications sent — explicitly descoped at Q19; the email itself is the entire deliverable.
- Any sharing, field-level-security, or licence change — explicitly descoped at Q15/Q18; the flow runs in automation context and needs no new user-facing visibility.

Tiered per skills/admin/fit-gap-analysis-against-org: the moment a Flow is in the delivery path the row is Low-Code, regardless of how simple the automation reads. |

## Decisions

| Id | Decision | Decision tree | Branch | ADR | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D1` | Build the notification as a Flow rather than relying on the native Escalation Rules engine's own notify actions, and rather than Apex. | `standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md` | Q4 |  | Q1 (record change) -> Q2 ('No' branch, since sending email and reading a related object crosses objects) -> Q4 asks whether the logic needs to cross objects (DML on related records, send email, create tasks); the answer is yes, which routes to Q5. Escalation Rules' own escalationAction (notifyTo/notifyEmail/notifyCaseOwner) targets a fixed user, role, or the case owner — read in skills/admin/escalation-rules/SKILL.md's Core Concepts table — and cannot dynamically resolve 'the Owner of the Case's related Account', so the native engine cannot satisfy this requirement regardless of whether escalation itself is already configured natively or manually. Apex is not warranted: none of automation-selection.md Q3's Apex triggers (governor-limit risk, retry/backoff callouts, complex rollback, recursive DML, coverage-gated deploy, custom exception types) apply to a single-record, single-email send. |
| `D2` | Use an After-Save record-triggered Flow on Case (Update only), firing inline (not on a Scheduled Path), rather than Before-Save. | `standards/decision-trees/flow-pattern-selector.md` | Q5 |  | flow-pattern-selector.md Q1 (record UPDATE) -> Q2 ('No', since the flow reads the related Account and sends email, not only same-record fields) -> Q4 (Yes, the action — sending email — must happen after the triggering DML commits) -> Q5 (No, the action is not time-relative to the record; the whole point of an escalation alert is that it fires now). Before-Save is structurally unable to send email or read a related record for anything beyond a lazy-loaded field lookup (skills/flow/record-triggered-flow-patterns Core Concepts, 'What before-save CANNOT do'). |

- `D1`
  - Branch quote: Q4. Does the logic need to cross objects (DML on related records, send email, create tasks)? ├── No → After-save record-triggered Flow └── Yes → Q5
  - Alternatives rejected: Native Escalation Rule notify action (notifyTo/notifyEmail); Apex trigger + handler
  - Consequences: The notification lives in Flow Builder, editable by an admin without a deploy for entry-criteria tweaks, but is a second place (besides any existing Escalation Rule) that reacts to IsEscalated — documented in the step note so a future admin does not assume Escalation Rules already cover this.
- `D2`
  - Branch quote: Q5. Does the action need to happen at a specific time RELATIVE to the record (e.g. "30 days after Close Date", "1 hour before SLA breach")? ├── Yes → After-Save record-triggered flow with Scheduled Path (entry criteria gates the schedule) └── No → After-Save record-triggered flow, firing inline
  - Alternatives rejected: Before-Save record-triggered Flow; After-Save with a Scheduled Path
  - Consequences: The email sends synchronously in the triggering transaction; a Send Email failure must be caught by a fault path (Q4) rather than retried later, since there is no scheduled path to fall back to.

## Milestones

### M1 — Email the Account Owner when a Case is escalated

Goal: Given a Case linked to an Account, when the Case transitions to IsEscalated = true (including a repeat escalation after being un-escalated), then an email is sent to the Account's Owner containing the Case Number and Subject; given the Case has no related Account, then no email is sent and the skip is logged; given the Account Owner is a Queue with no email, then the email is sent to the Support Manager distribution list instead; given the flow's Get-Owner or Send-Email step fails, then a fault-path log entry is written and the Salesforce admin distribution list is notified, with no unhandled fault.
